```{r}
#| eval: false
refloraR::reflora_parse()
```

### Description

Read Darwin Core Archive (DwC-A) files from any downloaded dwca
folder at [Reflora Virtual Herbarium](https://ipt.jbrj.gov.br/reflora/)
hosted by the [Rio de Janeiro Botanical Garden](https://www.gov.br/jbrj/pt-br).

### Details

Besides cleaning the taxonomic columns, `reflora_parse()` standardizes
the metadata that each herbarium fills in differently, so that the records
of different collections can be combined directly (e.g., with
`dplyr::bind_rows()`):

- `country` and `countryCode`: country names written in any of the languages found in the collections (e.g., "Brasil", "Bresil", "Alemanha", "E.U.A."), including common typos, are converted to English names (e.g., "Brazil", "Germany", "United States") and the missing ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes are filled in. A valid `countryCode` always takes precedence over the text. Placeholders (e.g., "?", "s.loc.", "Indeterminado") and text that is not a country become `NA`.
- `stateProvince`: for Brazilian records, state names are standardized to their official names (e.g., "Goias", "GO" and "Goyaz" become "Goiás"; "Minas Gerias" becomes "Minas Gerais"), including values corrupted by the source herbarium (accents exported as blanks or truncated names).
- `typeStatus`: English upper-case terms (e.g., "Holotipo" and "HOLOTYPUS" become "HOLOTYPE").
- `identificationQualifier`: "cf." and "aff.".
- `family`: the conserved alternative family names Labiatae, Umbelliferae, Compositae, Cruciferae, Gramineae, Leguminosae and Palmae are replaced by Lamiaceae, Apiaceae, Asteraceae, Brassicaceae, Poaceae, Fabaceae and Arecaceae.
- `year`, `month`, `day`, `decimalLatitude`, `decimalLongitude`, `minimumElevationInMeters` and `maximumElevationInMeters`: impossible values (e.g., month 1774, latitude 123456) are converted to `NA`. Both coordinates are blanked when either one is impossible.
- All text columns have leading, trailing and repeated blanks (including non-breaking spaces) removed, and empty strings become `NA`.
- Every herbarium is returned with the same columns, in the same order and with the same classes. Columns that a herbarium does not publish are filled with `NA`.

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| path | Pathway to the computer's directory, where the Reflora-downloaded dwca folders are. |
| herbarium | A vector of specific herbarium acronyms (collection code) in uppercase letters or leave it as `NULL` to parse specimen records for all herbarim dcwa folders in the defined path directory. |
| repatriated | Logical. If `FALSE`, skips downloading records from Reflora-associated herbaria that have been repatriated. Default is `TRUE`. Use `reflora_summary()` to check which collections are repatriated. Reflora aggregates collections from both Brazilian and international herbaria that hold Brazilian specimens. In this context, “digital repatriation” refers to making high-resolution images and associated specimen metadata openly accessible through a Brazilian public infrastructure (HVR/IPT). |
| verbose | Logical, if `FALSE`, a message showing steps when summarizing specimen records will not be printed in the console in full. |

### Value

A named list of Darwin Core Archive objects, one per parsed
herbarium collection. Each element corresponds to the output of
`finch::dwca_read()` and contains:

`$data`A list of data tables included in the archive,
including a cleaned and standardized `occurrence.txt` data frame
with selected Darwin Core fields.
`$meta`Metadata extracted from the archive's EML file.
`$files`Information about the archive structure and
associated files.

The returned list is named by herbarium collection codes. When available,
associated summary CSV files (generated by `reflora_download()`)
are appended as additional elements within each herbarium object.

### Examples

```r
reflora_download(herbarium = c("ALCB", "HUEFS", "K", "RB"),
                 verbose = TRUE,
                 dir = "reflora_download")

dwca <- reflora_parse(path = "reflora_download",
                      verbose = TRUE)
```
